name: Geodude
notes: item_299 (Geodude, grey-brown rock) should cluster with brown/tan/earthy, small-medium, natural Pokémon. It should be far from blue, dark, large, aggressive ones. The dominant grouping criterion appears to be primary color palette (brown/tan/earthy vs blue/green/dark) combined with size and aggression. Need to heavily boost brown_tan color weight, reduce blue color influence, and possibly add an earthy/natural color feature.

name: Wailord
notes: item_413 (Wailord) clusters with aquatic/shell Pokémon (item_320 Omanyte, item_094 Omastar, item_189) and plant-based (item_267 Gloom). Away from dark/menacing (item_323, item_370, item_097), mechanical (item_006), ice-spider (item_362), and rocky/grey (item_299). The grouping seems to be: natural soft-bodied aquatic/organic vs dark/mechanical/aggressive. Need to boost aquatic+shell combination, reduce blue color dominance, heavily penalize dark+menacing combination.

name: Swadloon
notes: The grouping criterion appears to be primarily GREEN-colored Pokémon. item_364 (Swadloon) clusters with other green Pokémon regardless of type: plant, dragon, insect, aggressive, aquatic - as long as they are dominantly green. Items to avoid are non-green: brown mammals, blue/ice birds, tan/sandy types. Need to heavily boost primary_color_green and reduce weights of features that split green Pokémon apart.

name: Tentacruel
notes: The grouping appears to be fossil/ancient sea creature Pokémon or invertebrate-type Pokémon with alien/non-vertebrate body plans. item_085 (jellyfish), item_320 (ammonite), item_189 (fossil manta), item_267 (mushroom-like), item_041 (alien humanoid), item_410 (plant), item_354 (rock). The common thread seems to be 'ancient/primordial/non-standard body type' - fossil Pokémon and their relatives. Need to boost is_ancient_fossil_type heavily and add a feature for non-standard/alien body morphology. Also need to reduce primary_color_green weight significantly since green was the previous hypothesis but seems wrong now.

name: Toxapex
notes: item_191 (large insect Pokémon with hard exoskeleton and spikes) should be in the same group as water mammals, fish, standard vertebrates, and common creatures - NOT with alien/fossil/plant/mineral/ghostly forms. The grouping seems to separate 'standard vertebrate or conventional creature types' (fish, mammals, birds, amphibians, reptiles, even large bugs that are recognizable) from 'weird/alien/fossil/plant/mineral/ghostly' types. I need to reduce alien_non_vertebrate_form weight since item_191 scores 1 there incorrectly affecting it. The key separator seems to be: does the Pokémon look like a recognizable real-world creature type (even if stylized) vs something truly weird/alien/fossil/mineral/plant-based. Need to add a feature for 'recognizable creature form' that captures insects/vertebrates together vs plant/mineral/ghost/anchor/fossil-alien forms.

name: Phanpy
notes: The grouping criterion appears to be primarily based on COLOR - specifically cool blue/teal/grey/dark colored Pokémon vs warm brown/tan/orange/red colored ones. item_018 (blue elephant) groups with blue metallic, blue fossil, blue plant Pokémon, NOT with brown mammals or brown birds. The previous animal-vs-plant/mineral hypothesis was completely wrong. Need to heavily weight blue/cool colors and de-weight the animal/plant/mineral/fossil type features.

name: Pumpkaboo
notes: The grouping criterion appears to be GREEN vs NON-GREEN. Items with significant green coloring (primary or secondary) are grouped together, while items without green are grouped together. item_053 (pumpkin - orange/brown, no green) should be away from all the green Pokémon. Need to heavily weight green features and reduce weight of cool/warm color features that were dominating.

name: Woobat
notes: The grouping appears to be GREEN vs NON-GREEN. item_322 (bat, no green) should cluster with other non-green items like item_267, item_041, item_410, item_189, item_320, item_080, item_354, item_202. Items it should be farther from (item_370, item_234, item_266, item_311, item_378, item_058, item_146, item_288, item_151) also have no green - suggesting a secondary criterion within non-green items. The green features need maximum weight, and I need to better distinguish sub-clusters. Perhaps cool-blue/teal coloring vs warm/pink coloring is the secondary split within non-green items.

name: Wynaut
notes: The grouping criterion is primarily COLOR TEMPERATURE/HUE: cool-toned Pokémon (blue, teal, green) vs warm-toned Pokémon (brown, tan, orange, red, pink). item_337 is blue/teal and belongs with blue/teal/green items. The green features were partially capturing this but the key distinction is cool (blue+teal+green) vs warm (brown+orange+red+tan). I need to heavily weight cool_color_palette and blue_teal_body_color, while also keeping green features, and downweight green-only features that miss the broader cool/warm split.

name: Dachsbun
notes: The grouping criterion appears to be: warm brown/tan+green natural earthy Pokémon vs cool blue/teal Pokémon vs warm red/orange Pokémon vs dark/pink Pokémon. item_246 (brown dog) groups with brown+green plant creatures. Need a feature capturing 'brown/tan body with green accents' as a combined signal, while reducing cool blue and pure green weights.

name: Carnivine
notes: item_344 is a green plant with no brown - should cluster with cool/teal items (item_058, item_097, item_311) NOT with brown+green items. The key discriminator is brown_tan_with_green: items with brown+green go together, while pure green (no brown) items go with cool/teal group. Need to heavily weight brown_tan_with_green and reduce standalone green features. The grouping seems to be: (1) brown+green earthy creatures, (2) cool blue/teal creatures, (3) warm red/orange, (4) pink/dark. Pure green without brown falls into cool group.

name: Mudsdale
notes: item_377 (brown horse, no green) groups with brown+green earthy creatures. The earthy group is defined by warm brown/tan dominant coloring, not requiring green. Groups: (1) warm brown/tan dominant (with or without green), (2) cool blue/teal, (3) warm red/orange/pink dominant, (4) dark/ghostly/other. Need to weight warm brown more heavily as a standalone feature, separate from the green requirement.

name: Clobbopus
notes: The grouping is by dominant color palette. Group 1: warm brown/tan/beige/cream dominant (item_242's cream body fits here). Group 2: cool blue/teal dominant. Group 3: warm red/orange dominant (not brown). Group 4: green dominant. Group 5: dark/black dominant. Group 6: pink/purple dominant. item_242 is cream/beige with orange spots - its body base is warm neutral/cream, grouping it with the warm brown/tan items. Need to make warm_brown_tan_body capture cream/beige as well.

name: Ivysaur
notes: Grouping is by dominant color. item_281 (Ivysaur) is green-dominant body, should be in green group not teal group. item_202 is teal/blue-dominant. Need green_dominant_body to strongly separate these. Increase weight on green_dominant_body, reduce cool_teal_no_brown slightly.

name: Panpour
notes: Grouping is by dominant color. item_351 (Ambipom) belongs to a cream/beige + blue group alongside item_320 (Omanyte), item_167 (Nosepass), item_094 (Kabuto), item_140 (Wailord), item_157 (Blastoise) - all share prominent cream/beige body coloring, often combined with blue accents. The cream_beige_body feature needs much higher weight. item_299 is grey/rock group. item_311 is pure blue. item_234 is pink. item_323 is dark. Need to strongly differentiate cream/beige from grey, dark, pink, and pure blue.

name: Gabite
notes: The grouping appears to be: cream/beige body with blue accents OR blue body with cream/beige secondary coloring. This is essentially the cream_beige_with_blue_accents group but also includes items like Salamence which has blue dominant body with cream/beige underbelly. The key shared trait is BOTH blue/teal AND cream/beige present on the body together. Need to boost cream_beige_with_blue_accents weight heavily and ensure it captures both directions (cream+blue AND blue+cream).

name: Tyrunt
notes: The grouping criterion appears to be warm brown/tan body color as the dominant feature. item_273 (Cranidos) and its neighbors are all Pokémon with predominantly warm brown, tan, beige, or earth-toned bodies. The current high-weight features (cream_beige_with_blue_accents, blue_and_cream_combo) are wrong for this group and need to be zeroed out. The key discriminating feature is warm_brown_tan_body.

name: Shaymin
notes: The grouping criterion appears to be green color presence / plant-based aesthetic. Items with significant green coloring (plant Pokémon, grass types, green-bodied Pokémon) cluster together. Blue/dark/aquatic Pokémon without green form a separate cluster. Need to heavily weight green_dominant_or_secondary and plant_based features, and reduce warm_brown_tan_body dominance.

name: Phantump
notes: The grouping criterion appears to be green color presence. Items with significant green (plant Pokémon, grass types) form one group; items without green (brown mammals, rock types, non-green plants, grey/dark animals) form another. item_160 has minimal green so belongs with non-green group. Need to heavily weight green features and reduce weight of plant_based (since non-green plants like item_160, item_274, item_047, item_267 sort into different groups based on green presence, not plant nature).

name: Volcanion
notes: The grouping criterion appears to be warm vs cool color palette. Warm-colored Pokémon (brown, tan, orange, red, red-orange, and brown+green combinations) form one group; cool-colored Pokémon (blue, teal, purple, grey, icy white) form another group. item_069 (red/dark) belongs with warm group alongside brown+green Pokémon. Pure green items with no brown may still be warm-side. Items with blue/teal bodies are cool side.

name: Scovillain
notes: The grouping criterion is green-dominant color palette vs non-green (warm brown/orange/tan/red or cool blue/grey). Green Pokémon (plant greens, teal-greens, dark greens) form one group; non-green Pokémon (warm browns, oranges, tans, reds, or cool blues without green) form another. item_381 is green-dominant despite having red heads. The key feature is whether green is the primary/dominant body color.

name: Palossand
notes: The grouping criterion appears to be color palette category: 1) GREEN dominant Pokémon, 2) NEUTRAL/MUTED Pokémon (grey, brown, tan, dark without vivid color), 3) WARM VIVID Pokémon (red, orange, yellow, pink dominant), 4) COOL VIVID Pokémon (blue, teal dominant). item_029 (sandy tan) groups with grey/dark/muted brown Pokémon, away from vivid red/orange, away from blue/cream fossils. The key distinction within non-green is muted/neutral vs vivid warm vs vivid cool.

name: Pidgeotto
notes: The grouping is by dominant color palette: 1) Brown/tan warm neutral Pokémon (including those with green accents - brown+green group), 2) Dark/black dominant, 3) Vivid warm (red/orange/pink/yellow), 4) Cool vivid (blue/teal). item_152 (Pidgeot) is brown/tan and belongs with the brown+tan group including those with green. The key is warm_brown_tan_body captures item_152, item_232, item_046, item_076, item_004, item_276, item_435.

name: Gloom
notes: The grouping separates items by color: 1) Warm brown/tan dominant, 2) Dark/black dominant, 3) Vivid warm (red/orange/pink), 4) Vivid cool blue/teal. item_267 has a muted/desaturated blue-grey body - it belongs with dark/muted group, NOT with vivid blue/teal. The key is that 311, 006, 370, 058, 151 have VIVID saturated blue/teal while 267, 249, 406 are dark/muted. Need to boost vivid blue/teal separation and add a feature for muted/desaturated blue-grey.

name: Pidgeot
notes: The user groups by: 1) Items with significant green coloring (green-dominant or brown+green combo) vs 2) Items without green. Within non-green: further split by color type (muted/grey/dark, warm brown/tan, vivid warm non-brown, vivid cool blue). item_024 is warm-brown bird with NO green - groups with other no-green items. The brown+green combo items (078, 122, 042, 404, 095, 204) form their own cluster separate from pure-brown/muted items. Need to heavily weight green presence as a separator.

name: Weedle
notes: item_150 (brown worm, no green) should be close to warm-brown items AND green+brown combo items, but far from cool blue/teal items and dark items. The grouping seems to be: warm-toned items (with or without green) vs cool/blue items vs dark items. Need to strongly weight warm vs cool separation, with green presence as secondary within warm group.

name: Greedent
notes: item_194 (brown squirrel) groups with muted natural-colored items (grey rock, brown+green animals) and away from vivid warm (red/yellow/pink), pastel/cream, or exotic cosmic items. The grouping criterion appears to be: muted/natural earth tones (brown, grey, brown+green) vs vivid warm colors (red/orange/pink/yellow) vs cool/dark/exotic. Need strong weight on muted_neutral_body and penalize vivid colors strongly.

name: Barbaracle
notes: item_055 (brown/grey rock humanoid with vivid green claws) groups with item_435 (brown bird with vivid green feathers). The criterion appears to be: warm brown/tan body combined with vivid/bright green elements. Away from: vivid red/orange (item_047, item_244, item_354), pink/magenta (item_288, item_266), dark-cool blue (item_298, item_315, item_430, item_406), cream/pastel (item_320), and blue+brown (item_267). The key feature is brown/tan + bright green combination. Need to strongly weight brown_tan_with_green and reduce weights on muted_earth_tone_body (which groups too many items together) and other features that conflate different color groups.

name: Whiscash
notes: item_217 (dark navy fish with cream underbelly and light blue accents) groups with item_094 (cream+blue fossil), item_320 (cream+blue shell), item_050 (cosmic/tan), item_354 (dark rock), item_410 (blue+green plant). Away from pink (288,266,234), vivid teal (311,370,6,58,151), grey rock (299), yellow (386), birds (113,378). The grouping criterion seems to be: cream/beige body combined with blue/teal accents OR dark muted non-vivid body - basically ancient/fossil aesthetic with mixed neutral+cool palette. Need to boost cream_beige_with_blue_accents and is_ancient_fossil_type, reduce cool_vivid features.

name: Decidueye
notes: item_435 (brown bird with green feathers) should group with warm brown/tan animals (mammals, birds with brown bodies), NOT with green-dominant Pokémon. The criterion seems to be primarily about warm brown/tan body color as the dominant feature, regardless of green accents. Need to heavily reduce brown_with_vivid_green and brown_tan_with_green weights, boost warm_brown_tan_dominant_body.
